newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australis says in talks about merger.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australis says in talks about merger.

text.p: Troubled pay television group Australis Media Ltd on Friday confirmed it was in general discussions with Optus Vision and Foxtel concerning the possibility of rationalisation in the pay television industry, including possible merger transactions.

"As requested by the (Australian Stock) Exchange in relation to ongoing press speculation, Australis confirms that general discussions are continuing between itself and OptusVision, Foxtel, and their respective principals, concerning the possibility of rationalisation in the pay television industry, including possible merger transactions," the company told the Australian Stock Exchange.
"Australis is unable to predict whether and, if so, how and when any such rationalisation will occur."
The nation's three key pay-tv operators are estimated to have lost a combined A$1 billion since last year's start-up.
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), the nation's anti-monopolies authority, rejected a merger proposal between Australis and Foxtel in late 1995.
Since then, Australis has been forced into a number of major capital raisings and restructurings, while discussing joint venture and infrastructure-sharing deals with Optus.
The infrastructure deal with Optus was rejected by the New South Wales Supreme Court on May 30 this year following a complaint from Foxtel.
Optus and Foxtel compete in the affluent sections of major cities while the satellite-based delivery of Australis is focussed nowadays on the perimeter of the capital cities and semi-rural regions.
Optus Vision is the pay television arm of Optus Communications Pty Ltd and has about 185,000 subscribers.

Optus Communications had held 46.5 percent but agreed with minority shareholders including Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd and Seven Network Ltd in late March to swap their pay-tv investments for a stake in Optus Communications.
Packer is also a major investor in Australis and was instrumental behind the company's financial restructuring late last year following a poor response to a large U.S. debt issue.
Australis last week announced a nine month net loss of A$199.49 million.

Foxtel is a joint venture between Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd and the Australian government's telecoms group Telstra Corp. They have agreed to a A$3.billion cable rollout to provide pay-tv throughout the country, with about 140,000 subscriber at the start of the yearq.
